editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a tiny prison cell with four strangers and nothing to do but eat bland food. That is exactly where Kenta finds himself. He is the new guy, and he is totally miserable with the prison meals. However, things get interesting on New Year's Day when the inmates get a special traditional meal. Instead of just eating, the group starts a wild game. They take turns bragging about the best meals they have ever had in their lives, and the winner gets to steal food from the others. It turns a gloomy jail cell into a battle of memories and tastes, making the whole vibe feel surprisingly warm and funny despite the setting.

You will love how the movie uses simple conversations to take you on a journey through different flavors and emotions. The acting is great because the characters feel like real people you might meet. While the plot is slow since it mostly takes place in one room, the stories they tell keep you hooked. If you want a cozy, feel-good comedy, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie ends with the group finishing their game and sharing a real bond over their memories. Kenta, who started off feeling lonely and grumpy, finally feels like he belongs with the other prisoners. The twist is that the food game was not really about winning, but about healing their hearts. They realize that the taste of home is what they miss most, and they end the film as true friends.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves food stories and heartwarming friendships.
